extracted.intended_audience: physical comedians, performers, film comedy directors, and students studying Buster Keaton-style slapstick
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for producing or assessing Buster Keaton–style physical comedy on film or stage: deadpan acting combined with precisely timed, dangerous physical gags filmed to show the full action. Emphasizes choreography, stunt technique, camera use, and comedic beat structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucidity and ballistic precision (style identifier)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Great Stone Face." Lucidity and precision + acrobatics of ballistic precision and kineticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keaton's style is defined by clarity of movement and the sense of the body as a precisely operating machine. Performances should read clearly to the audience: each action should have a lucid cause-and-effect and economical, athletic execution rather than sentimental or frantic exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan facial expression and 'slow burn' emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow burn mastery — emotion withheld, surfaces in micro-expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a largely unreactive, deadpan face while allowing tiny micro-expressions to puncture the surface at the right moment. This restrained emotional register distinguishes Keaton from sentimental (Chaplin) or frantic (Lloyd) performers and amplifies absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing precision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gravity, split-second timing, and physical props to make stunts look effortless. Sequences should be meticulously choreographed so every movement, fall, and leap contributes to the gag's crescendo. Poor timing (hesitation, rushed beats) kills the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical commitment and authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the physical commitment real (no fake)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keaton performed his own stunts and committed physically to danger; authenticity sells the gag. Avoid faked reactions or obvious safety padding when the intent is to convey real risk. Rehearse thoroughly so dangerous actions read as effortless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan face / unreactive expression (explicit rubric item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unresponsive face is integral: it undercuts danger and heightens comic contrast. Keep reactions minimal even amid chaos; allow subtle micro-expressions to register the human element without spoiling the machine-like performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gag combines physical risk with comic absence of harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the gag combine physical risk with comic absence of harm?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful Keaton gag sets up genuine-seeming danger and then subverts expectation by the performer 'surviving' in a surprising or absurd way. The perception of real stakes (death-defying precision) followed by lack of harm is central to the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera shows full action / single-take integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the camera show the full action (no edit cheating)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer single takes and wide coverage so the audience witnesses the entire stunt; avoid cutting to hide stunt construction. Camera placement should emphasize scale and spatial relationships (e.g., wide shots showing distances, obstacles). Edits that fake the stunt reduce the gag's power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falling technique
rubrics_metrics.description: "The secret is in landing limp and breaking the fall with a foot or a hand."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falls should be rehearsed so the performer appears limp on impact while using limbs to break the fall safely and artfully. The technique must look natural and effortless; it is often developed over long rehearsal periods and may take years to perfect before a climactic gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic beat structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedic Beats — Setup: establish ordinary scene. Disruption: physical force. Survival: comic absence of expected harm. Continuation: scene proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct gags as a sequence of beats: clearly establish normalcy, introduce an inciting physical disruption, demonstrate a survival or reversal that undercuts danger, and then continue as if routine. Each beat must be signaled and timed so the audience follows the causal logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dangerous precision and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stood in specific locations relying on precise timing; famous house-front gag and train stunts performed without doubles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many Keaton gags rely on exact spatial placement (e.g., standing where windows will fall, lining up with moving trains). Measure and rehearse positions carefully; minor misplacement can cause failure or injury. The on-screen sense of risk must be credible, which usually requires rigorous planning rather than improvisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual universality and enduring factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual humor crosses language. Body-as-machine vs. body-as-grace tension. Death-defying precision implies real stakes. Deadpan amplifies absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design gags that communicate physically and visually so they work for international audiences. Exploit the tension between mechanical precision and human grace; ensure stakes feel real yet are resolved comically. The combination of visual clarity, physical risk, and restrained reaction contributes to longevity.
